music_shell_guide_check_label: Practice shows the target keys lit; Check hides them, and only Check counts toward your skill scores
music_shell_guide_check_p1: Every scored drill has two modes. {practice} shows the targets on the keys, frets or pads, and you can hear it first. {check} hides them.
music_shell_guide_check_p2: Only Check runs change your skill scores. Playing a scale while it's lit up shows you can follow the lights. Playing it in Check shows you know it. Practice runs are saved and earn XP too.
music_shell_guide_check_p3: "{hear}" plays a demo. It's never scored.
music_shell_guide_connect_heading: MIDI, the MPC and the microphone
music_shell_guide_connect_p1: {midi} works in Chromium browsers. Plug in the keyboard, MPC or Aerophone and turn on MIDI once on {connect}. After that Woodshed reopens it on every visit. Name each device and choose the instrument it plays as.
music_shell_guide_connect_p2: {mpc} only sends pad notes while a computer keeps talking to it. Link the MPC on Connect and Woodshed keeps the link alive on every page. If your pads send the Akai Classic notes, pick that pad map there, or use Learn pads and hit each pad once.
music_shell_guide_connect_p3: {mic} is for guitar, ukulele and voice. It starts only when you press something that needs it, and it stops when the drill ends. Pick the input and echo cancellation on {connect}. The {tuner} is the fastest way to check it hears you.
music_shell_guide_connect_p4: If notes feel late, run a latency calibration in {settings}.
music_shell_guide_countin_note: Timed drills count you in first (set the count-in in the top bar). Nothing you play during the count-in is scored. Woodshed saves each run as you go.
music_shell_guide_devices_label: Keyboard, MPC and Aerophone connect over MIDI, the MPC with a heartbeat. The guitar comes in through the microphone
music_shell_guide_keys_p1: With no instrument nearby, the keys below play whichever surface is on screen. They follow key positions, so they work the same on other keyboard layouts.
music_shell_guide_nm_p1: Some inputs can't measure everything. An on-screen pad has no velocity. The microphone can't tell which string you used. A computer keyboard plays one note at a time, so it can't measure two hands together.
music_shell_guide_nm_p2: Then the results say {nm} for that part and leave it out of the score. You get neither a zero nor a free 100%. Connect the real instrument and those rows start counting.
music_shell_guide_octave_keys: {z} and {x} shift down or up an octave, three either way.
music_shell_guide_pad_one: Pad 1 is bottom left, the same as A01 on the MPC.
music_shell_guide_pads_caption: MPC pads, laid out like the pad grid
music_shell_guide_pads_map: Pad key map: Z X C V play pads 1 to 4 on the bottom row, then A S D F, Q W E R, and 1 2 3 4 on the top row for pads 13 to 16.
music_shell_guide_piano_map: Piano key map: A S D F G H J K L play the white keys from C4 to D5; W E, T Y U, O P play the black keys.
music_shell_guide_privacy_label: Sessions, scores, recordings and samples stay inside this browser. Nothing goes to a server
music_shell_guide_privacy_p1: Everything stays in this browser: sessions, scores, recordings and samples. There's no account, and nothing goes to a server. Woodshed analyses microphone sound on this device and saves it only when you record a take.
music_shell_guide_privacy_p2: Clearing this site's data in the browser deletes it, so make a backup in {settings} now and then. Backups are files you keep.
music_shell_guide_result_label: A result card: notes right 92 percent, timing 78 percent, velocity not measured on an on-screen pad
music_shell_guide_ringed: The ringed block, marked Next, is the one Start plays.
music_shell_guide_sc_search: Search every drill, path, song and page. {ctrl} {k} on Windows and Linux. Arrow keys move, Enter goes.
music_shell_guide_sc_space: Start a drill, or run it again from the results, while focus isn't on a button or field.
music_shell_guide_set_label: Today's set: four five-minute blocks, scales, ear, reading and rhythm, with the first one ready to start
music_shell_guide_step_1: Open Today and pick how many minutes you have.
music_shell_guide_step_2: Woodshed builds a short set from what's due: something you're learning, something slipping, something to review.
music_shell_guide_step_3: Press Start and go block by block. Woodshed remembers the setup, so most days that's all it takes.
music_shell_guide_step_4: Each run ends with one sentence, your score, the change since last time, and what to try next.
music_shell_guide_streaks_p1: Your streak counts the days you practise in a row. Every week you practise earns a {freeze}, and you can hold two. Miss a day and a freeze covers the gap. Frozen days show dashed on the week calendar.
music_shell_guide_streaks_p2: {xp} rewards showing up: a wrong answer still earns a little, a hard clean run earns much more, and beating your last run adds a bonus. Every 250 XP is an XP level.
music_shell_guide_streaks_p3: XP isn't skill. Skill scores are separate: only Check runs change them, and they fade when you leave a skill alone. That's how Progress knows what's due.
